flawed_step: The hypotheses do not force a Hamiltonian cycle.
counterexample: Let G=K_{2,4}, with bipartition {u,v} and {a,b,c,d}, and edges ux and vx for each x in {a,b,c,d}. It is simple and connected. Degrees are deg(u)=deg(v)=4 and deg(a)=deg(b)=deg(c)=deg(d)=2, so it is Eulerian. Deleting u or v leaves a connected star; deleting any of a,b,c,d leaves K_{2,3}, which is connected. Thus G is 2-connected. But every cycle in a bipartite graph contains equally many vertices from each part, whereas the parts of G have sizes 2 and 4, so no cycle can contain all six vertices. Hence G is not Hamiltonian.
assessment_summary: The explicit graph K_{2,4} satisfies every hypothesis but violates the conclusion.
